System Suitability and QC

Source: vignettes/system-suitability.Rmd
system-suitability.Rmd

Scope

The SEC QC functions calculate resolution, plate count, asymmetry, recovery, and replicate precision from supplied peak data. The acceptance criteria are provided by the analyst or taken from the function’s defaults; they are not selected or validated by the package.

sec_system_suitability is a synthetic teaching dataset. Its expected_* columns are generated scenario values, not metrics calculated from the raw traces. The dataset contains a sequence of column-age scenarios, not replicate injections, so it cannot show repeatability.

Synthetic column-age example 

library(measure.sec)
#> Loading required package: measure
#> Loading required package: recipes
#> Loading required package: dplyr
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dplyr'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'recipes'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     step
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
data(sec_system_suitability, package = "measure.sec")

run_summary <- sec_system_suitability |>
  distinct(
    run_id,
    column_age_days,
    expected_plate_count,
    expected_resolution
  ) |>
  arrange(column_age_days)

run_metrics <- run_summary |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(expected_plate_count, expected_resolution),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "expected_value"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    metric = recode(
      metric,
      expected_plate_count = "Expected plate count (N, plates)",
      expected_resolution = "Expected resolution (Rs)"
    )
  )

run_metrics
#> # A tibble: 10 × 4
#>    run_id     column_age_days metric                           expected_value
#>    <chr>                <dbl> <chr>                                     <dbl>
#>  1 SST-Day0                 0 Expected plate count (N, plates)        45000  
#>  2 SST-Day0                 0 Expected resolution (Rs)                    2.8
#>  3 SST-Day30               30 Expected plate count (N, plates)        43000  
#>  4 SST-Day30               30 Expected resolution (Rs)                    2.7
#>  5 SST-Day60               60 Expected plate count (N, plates)        40000  
#>  6 SST-Day60               60 Expected resolution (Rs)                    2.5
#>  7 SST-Day90               90 Expected plate count (N, plates)        36000  
#>  8 SST-Day90               90 Expected resolution (Rs)                    2.3
#>  9 SST-Day120             120 Expected plate count (N, plates)        32000  
#> 10 SST-Day120             120 Expected resolution (Rs)                    2

The dashed lines below use the current default values in measure_sec_suitability() for plate count and resolution. They show how the software compares values with supplied criteria; they are not regulatory limits or a qualification decision.

criteria_lines <- tibble::tibble(
  metric = c(
    "Expected plate count (N, plates)",
    "Expected resolution (Rs)"
  ),
  value = c(5000, 1.5)
)

ggplot(run_metrics, aes(x = column_age_days, y = expected_value)) +
  geom_blank(
    data = criteria_lines |> mutate(column_age_days = 0),
    aes(x = column_age_days, y = value),
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(group = metric, colour = "Synthetic scenario"),
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = "Synthetic scenario"), size = 2) +
  geom_hline(
    data = criteria_lines,
    aes(yintercept = value, colour = "Software default"),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = NULL,
    values = c(
      "Synthetic scenario" = "#2E86AB",
      "Software default" = "#A23B72"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Column age in synthetic example (days)",
    y = "Generated scenario value"
  ) +
  theme_measure_sec()

Generated plate-count and resolution values across the synthetic column-age scenarios. Dashed lines mark the current default criteria in measure_sec_suitability(); they are included to explain the comparison, not to claim method acceptance.

Calculating suitability from an integration table

measure_sec_suitability() accepts a peak table with retention times and widths. If named reference peaks are supplied, it calculates resolution; it also calculates plate count from the selected main peak. Tailing, recovery, and replicate RSD are reported when the corresponding input columns or arguments are present.

The function’s current defaults are resolution at least 1.5, plate count at least 5,000, tailing factor from 0.8 to 1.5, recovery from 95% to 105%, retention-time RSD at most 1%, and area RSD at most 2%. These are software defaults. Select criteria for the method and review the width definitions and calculation conventions before using the output.

# Replace these objects with the integration table and criteria for your method.
sst <- measure_sec_suitability(
  peaks = integration_peak_table,
  reference_peaks = critical_peak_names,
  criteria = method_criteria
)

print(sst)

Repeatability requires replicate injections

measure_sec_suitability() can calculate retention-time and peak-area RSD when the peak table includes a replicate column and named peaks. The synthetic column-age dataset has no replicate injections, so those RSD values cannot be calculated from it. Pass replicate-level integration results when evaluating precision; keep missing results as missing rather than replacing them with zero.

# The table must contain actual repeated injections with peak-level values.
precision_results <- measure_sec_suitability(
  peaks = replicate_peak_table,
  reference_peaks = critical_peak_names,
  criteria = method_criteria
)

precision_results$results$retention_rsd
precision_results$results$area_rsd
